title: The effect of insufficient artificial lighting on workers' moods and physiology: preliminary research
research_question: To observe the effect of artificial light below the recommended illuminance levels for the workplace on workers' moods and their physiological condition.

participants.description: Five male printing employees, average 25.8 years old, working in a basement office in Sleman Regency, Special Region of Yogyakarta, Indonesia. Participants were observing Ramadhan fasting during the study.
participants.recruitment: Not explicitly stated, but they were existing employees in a real workplace.

stimuli_or_exposures.description: A basement office with down-light-direct-lighting, illuminance level of 250 lx, and Correlated Color Temperature (CCT) of 5300 K. This lighting was below the recommended standard of 750 lx for printing activities. The basement also received limited natural lighting.

findings.quote: The questionnaire results' graph did not show a significant difference either in the morning or afternoon.

findings.consequent: Worker's mood based on physiological data
findings.quote: It can be concluded that insufficient lighting in workplace may not be suitable for maintaining worker's mood based on physiological data.

findings.antecedent: Insufficient artificial lighting (250 lx, 5300 K CCT, below recommended standard)
findings.mechanism: A low cortisol concentration can be interpreted as an increase in the hormone melatonin that leads to a decrease in alertness.
findings.quote: a low cortisol concentration can be interpreted as an increase in the hormone melatonin that leads to a decrease in alertness.

mechanisms: Insufficient lighting leads to drastically decreased cortisol levels, which can be interpreted as an increase in melatonin, subsequently leading to decreased alertness.
moderators: Hawthorn effect (potential influence on self-report measures)
implementation_implications: Insufficient lighting in the workplace may not be suitable for maintaining workers' mood and alertness based on physiological data, despite no subjective complaints.
limitations: The number of research subjects (n=5) was too small to provide strong evidence for the conclusion.
Fasting conditions (Ramadhan) were not considered in previous similar studies and may have influenced hormone concentrations.
The study did not include a performance test, which would have yielded a greater quantity of valid data.
Observations were limited to the initial 2 hours and the last 2 hours of working time, resulting in an incomplete cortisol trend curve.

paper_metadata.crossref_title: The effect of insufficient artificial lighting on workers’ moods and physiology: preliminary research
paper_metadata.crossref_journal: IOP Conference Series: Earth and Environmental Science
paper_metadata.crossref_abstract:
Abstract
               In line with the sustainability issue, the current research related to lighting has been focused on maintaining the health and well-being of the workers, not only for energy saving considerations. This preliminary research observed the effect of artificial light below the recommended illuminance levels for the workplace on the workers’ moods and their physiological condition. The researchers employed a quasi-experimental approach by observing the participants’ sleepiness state, mood, and physiological condition related to their cortisol levels in the first two and last two hours of their work shift. The research subjects were five male printing workers who worked in the basement of an office building in Sleman Regency, Special Region of Yogyakarta, Indonesia. As the room was below the ground floor, to accommodate their work activities, the employees relied on artificial lighting, complemented by a small amount of natural lighting entering the basement. The lighting was measured on the illuminance level of 250s lx and the CCT of 5000s K. The research revealed that there is no complaint or problem regarding the illuminance level, no effect on the individuals’ state of sleepiness, or on their moods. However, the cortisol level tended to decrease faster than the normal circadian curve. Therefore, it is reasonable to conclude that even though ‘insufficient’ lighting levels can accommodate activities, the physiological condition of the subjects shows different results which indicate a negative increment.
